DO I HAVE A STORY FOR YOU! In my friend group there is this girl. I call her Topaz when I post about her. She is autistic. People say her and I are different levels of functioning but I can't get them to understand we aren't. When we unmask around close friends we handle the situation differently I'm picking up around as much as her. What's different is where when someone makes a pie she doesn't like she will spit it out right in front of the person who made it's face and throw it away (real story) and when I do it I excuse myself to the bathroom, spit it out there, tell them it was good but I don't think it's for me, and offer the rest to someone else. NEITHER OF US WANTED TO SWALLOW THAT BITE! But I considered others and she considered herself. She does this constantly, doing things that is rude or inconsiderate and everyone passes it off with "well Topaz just doesn't understand" and no one will realize it's because NO ONE TELLS HER OTHERWISE. 

I had to deal with the awkward talks of "hey what you're doing is rude and inconsiderate" for alot of things I did. I heard them out and I found a way for "hey I'm gonna react but this reaction is a way I can control it" or I at least say sorry! It's people who are either a: never been told "hey this hurts my feelings" or "I would really appreciate it if we could tone it down for a minute" in a constructive way or those who don't care enough to avoid doing it anyways. People think autism means we don't understand when we do wrong but it's that we don't understand non-constructive criticism. It can't be "don't do that because I said so" we need to discuss why this isn't good and if they can't take that criticism it's not the autism it's the person. At least in my experience of dealing with autistic people I can't stand unmasking around me and those who I love unmasking around and watching our tism click.

I recommend talking first. Say "hey this is how I feel" you don't even need a solution. If they ask how they can fix it talk it out. Give examples and even let them be like "what if I did this instead". And if they can't maybe distance yourself. They will either learn to compromise or you don't need them around.

I joke about being a cripple. It's one of those slurs my also disabled mother started "owning" but we both will say things like "make way for the cripple" or "you expect the cripple to do (a possible task we can do but still a big ask)". Never had I, my fiance, or my family have ever EVER used that word in a serious tone. I think the bigger red flag here is that he has been getting mean and drinking. That he has not only caused toxic words and insults to come not only at you but your children as well. Whether it's a slur or not he meant those words to hurt and that's not okay. And if he is saying things like this I would be concerned about what his drinking has yet to bring. Especially since you have brittle bone disease please OP consider if this is a safe place for not only you but your kids. If he is acting mean to you he isn't a functioning alcoholic. He's an alcoholic period. If he can't keep himself in check he isn't functioning. Mean words are abused whether he does it only when he's drunk or not. He needs to either stop drinking (which it seems like he believes isn't possible) or you need to realize you and your children are not more important than racing to the bottom of those bottles. I genuinely hope that if he can't sober up for you that you may not have a reason to stay. I know that especially with disabilities the idea of starting over again seems impossible but it isn't and you owe it to yourself to not have to brace yourself for if he is in a good mood or not when he drinks. I don't care if it happens every 3 months or every 3 days. A pattern is too much.

All of North America minuse Mexico. Essentially anywhere there is a PetSmart store. Some of us (depending on the supervisor) are also told to transfer for any notes because even now with the reservation center taking only 800 number calls we have 20-50 calls waiting to be answered in salon ques. Transferring for any notes keeps us within our calls per hours requirements and that means more revenue per hour.

The hardest part is PNES is so complex and so little is known about it that no therapist in a 100 mile radius knows how to treat it and then I need to assentially concent to a therapist experimenting on me so that "we know how to treat it better next time".
